edition.notes: A dated official English delivery state carrying the complete instruction, nn. 1-133, with its dates (28 March 2001, published 7 May 2001) and the signatures of Cardinal Jorge A. Medina Estevez and Archbishop Francesco Pio Tamburrino. The Latin published in Acta Apostolicae Sedis 93 (2001) 685-726 is the authoritative text and is not registered here. Later instruments modified the translation regime: Francis's motu proprio Magnum principium (3 September 2017) amended canon 838, and this record makes no claim about the instruction's present force.

passages.context: The instruction's own chapter on the publication of liturgical books, read at nn. 110-118 on 2026-08-01. Two numbers settle the question this repository kept relitigating. n. 111: 'As regards the liturgical books of the Roman Rite promulgated in an editio typica either before or after the Second Vatican Council by decree of the Congregations competent at the time, the Apostolic See, through the Administratio Patrimonii or, in its name and by its mandate, through the Libreria Editrice Vaticana, possesses and reserves to itself the right of ownership commonly known as "copyright". The granting of permission for a reprinting pertains to the Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments.' n. 117: 'The rights of publication and the copyright for all translations of liturgical books, or at least the rights in civil law necessary for exercising complete liberty in publishing or correcting texts, is to remain with the Conferences of Bishops or their national liturgical Commissions.' n. 118 provides for a licensing agreement where the copyright in a translation is common to several Conferences, which is the case of the English. n. 110 lists the books in view and names the Missale Romanum first. The consequence for a translator is stated by the two together: the Latin is claimed, and the English is claimed, and they are claimed by different parties.
passages.notes: The same exact bytes as the complete-text passage on this edition, refetched on 2026-08-01 and found byte-identical to the 2026-07-25 acquisition, so the two passages cannot come apart. An English delivery state and not the promulgated Latin. An ecclesiastical instruction is also not a civil-law adjudication: it states what the Holy See and the Conferences claim and directs how they are to act, and a court in any given jurisdiction would still decide what subsists and in whom it vests.

passages.context: The complete English delivery was read. Numbers material to translation method were checked at their own loci: n. 20 (translation is not creative innovation but integral and most exact rendering, without paraphrase or gloss); n. 25 (easily understandable language preserving dignity, beauty and doctrinal precision); n. 27 (the voice of the Church at prayer, free of overly servile adherence to prevailing modes of expression, tending to a sacred vernacular style); n. 51 (varied Latin vocabulary should yield varied vernacular vocabulary); n. 53 (Latin terms of rich meaning, naming munus, famulus, consubstantialis, propitius); n. 56 (expressions of the ancient Church's heritage to be translated as literally as possible, naming Et cum spiritu tuo and mea culpa, mea culpa, mea maxima culpa); n. 57 (the Roman Rite's concise manner of expression to be maintained); n. 64 and n. 74 (stability of memorized and sung texts; where larger conformity changes are necessary they should be made at one time with catechesis).

work.description: The fifth instruction for the right implementation of Sacrosanctum Concilium, dated 28 March 2001 and published 7 May 2001, governing vernacular translation of the Roman liturgical books. Numbered 1-133 with appendices. It is the stated norm under which the third typical edition of the Roman Missal was translated into English.
